name: reading-experience
description: Reusable browser-level check definitions for the five-story reading experience. Elara runs these as page checks against the loopback-only production server (npm start, http://127.0.0.1:3000). Every route is checked at each viewport: the skip-link keyboard flow, the server-rendered reading progress (exactly one aria-current link, the exact 'Story N of 5' position, the next-story cue or the story-five ending), the landmarks, evidence and citation rendering, and clean console, request and scroll behaviour. This file remains reusable browser-check definition data that Elara's page checks consume: the browser steps run only as Elara page checks. npm run verify:reading (scripts/verify-reading.mjs) starts and stops its own loopback production server and checks the five server-rendered HTTP responses for the essential story content, local illustrations, citations, disclaimers, ordinary navigation links, and the correct current-page state, using the serverContract object below; it never executes page JavaScript and never launches a browser, and those checks are safeguards, not proof of complete no-JavaScript browser behaviour or WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.

serverContract.description: The server-rendered reading contract that scripts/verify-reading.mjs enforces over plain HTTP. The script starts and stops its own loopback production server (npm start), fetches all five routes without executing JavaScript or launching a browser, and checks each response: exactly one main#main-content with exactly one h1 (heading) and a body paragraph, the title substrings in the document <title>, at least one local illustration (imageSrcPrefix) that answers HTTP 200 with an image content type, at least one https:// citation anchor inside main, the visible disclaimer, the header nav with exactly the five story links in reading order, exactly one aria-current on this route's link, the 'Story N of 5' label, the skip link before the header, and a main time with a datetime. Story 5 carries endingState and visibleStrings and no next-story link; stories 1 to 4 carry a next-story cue to the following route. Where this object is incomplete the script falls back to its built-in copy of the same contract, so the enforced contract never weakens.

unverifiedGaps.check: Skip-link flow, progress rendering, zoom, reflow and navigation in native Safari on macOS and iOS (the documented supported browser, not WebKit in general).
unverifiedGaps.note: WebKit is not native Safari: a WebKit-engine result is not represented here as native Safari coverage.

unverifiedGaps.check: Screen reader navigation: landmark and heading structure, the skip link, and the reading-progress cue announced correctly with assistive technology.
200% page zoom: content stays readable, the skip link still reaches main, and no sideways scrolling appears at or beyond the viewport widths above.
Reflow at viewport widths and aspect ratios beyond the listed widths (320, 375, 768, 1280, 1920 px).

notes: Browser behaviour is exercised only by Elara page checks against the loopback production server; this file is data, not an executable test, and nothing in it runs under a Node script.

npm run verify:reading (scripts/verify-reading.mjs) is a Node-only loopback HTTP safeguard: it starts and stops its own loopback production server (npm start) and checks the five server-rendered HTTP responses for the essential story content, local illustrations, citations, disclaimers, ordinary navigation links, and the correct current-page state, using the serverContract object above. It never executes page JavaScript and never launches a browser, and its results are safeguards, not proof of complete no-JavaScript browser behaviour or WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
